posts.title: Sales changed the buy.
posts.x:
A sale should change the supply plan.

BUY HARD passed a local Square Sandbox test: 60 gift sets sold, 60 boxes consumed, a 125-box buy planned. No supplier purchase.
https://buyhard.app/walkthrough?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=buyhard_allgas_202609&utm_content=square_test_result

posts.linkedinTagged:
A small working step toward staying stocked.

In a local Square Sandbox test, a completed test order for 60 gift sets reduced projected shipping-box stock by 60 and produced a plan to buy 125 boxes.

When Square sent the order notifications again, BUY HARD recognized the already-counted sale. One sale, one stock change.

This was a development test, not a customer order or a supplier purchase. Shopify is connected to a development store too; its order-to-stock test is still ahead.

The goal: the sales you already record should help your buyer keep supplies ready. Bring one recurring item to a walkthrough:
https://buyhard.app/walkthrough?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=buyhard_allgas_202609&utm_content=square_test_result

The supplier says Thursday. You needed it Tuesday.

What if your buyer caught that delay, checked how long your remaining stock would last, and brought you another option?

That's a direction for BUY HARD. Fewer last-minute calls. A clearer decision before the shelf is empty.

A delivery doesn't always arrive all at once.

You ordered 20 cases. Twelve arrive today; eight are still outstanding.

BUY HARD supports recording a partial delivery against the purchase, keeping the remaining quantity in view. The next buying decision should account for what arrived and what's still expected.

The numbers on this card are illustrative, not a customer shipment.
